gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.title: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind - Agentic Governance
gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_08_14_the_ai_briefing_by_start.summary: Gary's Guide: The AI Briefing is a high-velocity roundtable for decision-makers brought to you by Startup Grind. We bypass the hype by dissecting one high-signal industry deck with a room of vetted founders, operators, & enterprise executives. No lectures-just a 60-minute deep-dive into the tactics & data defining your next quarter. The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise. This Month's Source: The AI Agent Governance Gap: What CISOs Need Now (Cloud Security Alliance AI Safety Initiative - Apr 2026) Gartner projects that 40% of enterprise applications will embed task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025. However, it's becoming clear that governance hasn't kept pace with that curve. A 2026 survey of CISOs & CIOs at large enterprises found that 92% of them lack full visibility into their own AI agent identities. 95% doubt they could detect or contain a compromised agent if one turned up. That leaves a real gap for enterprises deploying agents today. No enforceable standard exists yet, & the frameworks most organizations already lean on (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, the EU AI Act) were built for AI that responds to a prompt, not for AI that plans & takes action across outside systems on its own. The Mission: Who owns the agent when it acts? This session is co-hosted with Lazy 8 AI, an engineering collective focused on the transition from manual coding to managing autonomous AI systems. We'll use the report's own gaps, especially around identity & incident response, as the anchor for a broader conversation: what readiness actually looks like when the standards bodies are still a year or more behind the deployments. The Format: We'll open with the numbers: 92% of CISOs & CIOs blind to their own agent identities, & a standards timeline that leaves them on their own well into 2026. The room debates the report's own recommendations: agent inventories, least-privilege credentials, agent-specific incident response. What's realistic for a team that's already stretched, & what's closer to theater. Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Understand the exposure your organization is carrying right now, before a standard exists to measure against, & what following best practice will need to mean when a regulator or a board comes knocking. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on what you're actually doing today to track agent identity, permissions, & incident response, & where the gap between what leadership assumes & what's built is widest. Founders & Builders: See where the governance tooling gap is actually a product opportunity, & why the report's own commercial incentives should make you skeptical of framework adoption as the automatic answer. The Prep: This is a working session. Review the report here. Bring your perspective.

gary_2026_08_15_nj_code_coffee_meetup.title: NJ Code & Coffee Meetup
gary_2026_08_15_nj_code_coffee_meetup.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_08_15_nj_code_coffee_meetup.summary: Gary's Guide: Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly NJ Code & Coffee tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus! Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious). That includes operators, founders, & investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... all are welcome! People of all skill & experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, & many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you! Come grab a cup of coffee & meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, make friends! Agenda: 2pm: Doors open, networking starts 2:30pm: Intro circle 3pm: networking continues 5pm: event ends The Intro Circle Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle: We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, & logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says: *your name & job title/ role in tech/ tech stack, What you can help others with, *What you would like help with, Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool. After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized. Community Discord - come hang out before & after!: www.codeandcoffee.chat The Venue Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming & a powerful network. Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, & a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate & build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

gary_2026_08_19_junto_founder_dinner.summary: Gary's Guide: Hi, Andrew Yeung here. We started the Junto Founder Dinner series two years ago to bring together the top founders + builders. Each month, we invite 24 vetted early-stage founders & CEOs for a 3-hour, multiple-course dinner experience. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders A dinner experience designed to facilitate new connections & conversations, with rotating 6-person table formats Meaningful connections with ambitious peers solving similar problems If you're wondering how our dinners usually go... read this Our only intent is to bring good, smart humans together. Details: Date: Aug 19, 2026 Time: 6:00pm - 8:30pm Venue: Private Dinner Club in NYC Past attendees of my events include the founders/C-suite of Venmo, Duolingo, Foursquare, Lyft, Goldman Sachs, Compass, Superhuman, Yext, OpenDoor, Chief, LearnVest, DocSend, Vercel, Loom, Morning Brew, The Hustle, Gas, Teachable, Replit, Twitter, Slack, Pinterest, Yahoo, MongoDB, Business Insider, Wonder, Hinge. Apply to join by filling out the RSVP form. About our Hosts & Sponsors: Andrew Yeung is the founder of Fibe & The Shortlist NYC. He is also an angel investor & Partner at Next Wave NYC, a pre-seed venture fund. Andrew has hosted over 300 events for 50,000 founders, operators, investors, & tech professionals that were featured by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fast Company, Fortune Magazine, Axios, Newsweek, & Forbes. Business Insider dubbed him the "Gatsby of Silicon Alley." Hubble is NYC's largest online platform for startup office space. We combine Kayak-style browse & search, with our free advisory service that does all the heavy lifting: recommendations, shortlisting, booking tours & negotiating the best rates. Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups. With banking set up in minutes, 2% cashback cards, & powerful tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused-with support that goes to the ends of the earth to help you win. Fidelity brings certainty to startup founders & leaders with our automated cap table & equity management platform. No matter where you are on your journey, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Looking for an alternative to your current equity management solution? Our team will guide you through a smooth transition to our platform. Learn more. Get on the list for future events: Twitter Instagram Website

gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.title: Fundraising Launchpad - Early-Stage AI Startups
gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_08_19_fundraising_launchpad_ea.summary: Gary's Guide: Are you building an AI startup & preparing to raise capital? The Fundraising Launchpad helps early-stage AI founders in New York City prepare for fundraising by evaluating the strength of their technology & connecting the most promising startups with investors. Through the techtrust.ai Technology Trust framework, your startup receives a (confidential) Technology Trust Score that highlights the credibility, defensibility, & maturity of your AI technology. Selected startups are invited to a 15-minute pitch & evaluation session with the techtrust.ai team, designed to help you sharpen your fundraising story. Top startups are then introduced directly to our VC & angel partners as part of curated AI deal flow. How it works 1.Apply Apply your AI startup for the event via our form: https://tinyurl.com/ytmnu6dj 2.Technology Trust Score Your startup receives a confidential Technology Trust Score. 3.Founder Session Selected startups join the 15-minute pitch & evaluation session on Aug 19 at 6PM with the techtrust.ai team in NYC. 4.Investor Introductions Top startups are forwarded & introduced to our VC & angel partners. Spots are limited.

jc_culture_39177_2026_08_15_west_indian_.summary: County Commissioner Bill O’Dea and Chico Ramchal along side the West Indian American Committee will be holding a West Indian Family Fun Day at Lincoln Park, on August 15th, 2026 beginning at 11am and concluding at 8:00pm. This event is intended to provide a day and location where families of a West Indian background of Hudson County can congregate and celebrate their culture. It will also provide an insight to experience the West Indian culture if you are from any descent. Among culture sharing the committee will provide a host of community games for all age groups. Some of these activities include a tug-o-war, 100m race, sack race, etc. In conjunction with the activities, we will have a show mobile on location that will provide music and non-band performances, such as cultural dancing. The expected turnout is estimated at, with the committee providing over 50 volunteers to help support the event.
